findings.title: The new helper `items` returns only the sum of item cents (delivery is added by `total`), so its generic name invites a future mistaken use as an order total.
The change replaced the valid `Date.now()` with `Date.current()`, which is not a function on the Date constructor, so the component throws instead of rendering a time.

The ping target is now taken from the untrusted `host` query parameter instead of a fixed gateway, so any caller who can reach the handler can make the server send ICMP/DNS to an arbitrary host, and the `--` separator only stops option injection, not target selection.

The new `--` argument before the host assumes the container's ping implementation parses `--` as an end-of-options marker; BusyBox-based ping (common in minimal images) treats `--` as the target itself, so the requested host is silently ignored and `--` is pinged instead.

On success only the last line of ping output is returned, which drops the `--- statistics ---`, packet-loss and transmit lines, so the code looks like it handles multi-line output but actually discards the diagnostic data an operator needs.
The host query parameter is interpolated directly into a shell command string, giving remote shell command execution.
Wrapping the ping in a pipeline makes err reflect tail's exit status, so the http.Error branch at line 12 is effectively unreachable for ping failures.
The change removes the single fixed target and accepts any host, so callers can select which hosts the service probes.
Replacing the integer `id` query parameter with `name` silently breaks every existing caller of the endpoint, which now receives 400 'bad name'.
Dropping the forced `%d.pdf` suffix means the endpoint now serves any file inside reportsDir, not just PDFs.
The `IsLocal` guard is documented-safe for lexical traversal, but the handler comment or check should note/cover symlink traversal inside reportsDir.
Download now serves an attacker-controlled path with no validation, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files readable by the process (e.g. ?name=../secret).
The change drops the id-to-filename contract, so the endpoint now exposes any filename under reportsDir rather than only numeric <id>.pdf reports.
ByAuthor builds its query by interpolating the untrusted author argument into SQL with fmt.Sprintf, so the query text is controlled by the caller.

Preview now serves the fetched upstream body under the upstream's Content-Type (text/html for the allowed video-site URLs) instead of the fixed text/plain of BASE, so attacker-chosen URL paths render foreign HTML/JS on the application's own origin.
The outbound fetch has no timeout and does not inherit the incoming request's context, so a slow upstream URL can hold the handler and connection indefinitely even after the client gives up.

The allowlist compares only the parsed hostname, so ports are unrestricted and only names that literally match the fixed map are blocked, leaving address-level SSRF checks (resolved IP, private/link-local ranges) to DNS.
The 1 MiB cap is applied without any indication that the body was cut off, so a truncated response is indistinguishable from a complete one and the magic 1<<20 has no stated reason.
Preview fetches an arbitrary caller-supplied URL, so the endpoint is an SSRF primitive against anything the server can reach.
Copying resp.Header.Get("Content-Type") while returning attacker-controlled body content lets a remote origin serve HTML/JS from the application's own origin.
The fetch has no timeout: a slow or non-responding origin can hold the handler goroutine open indefinitely.
Upstream status codes and the io.Copy error are ignored, so failed or truncated fetches are reported to the caller as successful deliveries.
isPrintable accepts non-ASCII letters/digits and digit-leading names, so formatLabel emits them unquoted and a downstream ASCII label-name grammar may reject output that the base always quoted.
isPrintable is misnamed for what it checks, which invites a future caller to use it as a general printability test.
IDs returns a nil slice when users is empty (var out []string), which serializes to null in JSON and differs from an empty slice some callers may expect.
In the new `Range` function the local variable `stats` shadows the imported `stats` package used by the neighbouring `Summary` function.
Median sorts its argument in place, so a caller's slice is silently reordered and the shown test builds a fresh literal per case, so a mutation of the caller's data is never noticed.
The doc comment on Median documents only the return value, not the in-place reordering of xs, so a future caller may pass a slice it still needs.

SetMaxRetries mutates the package-level maxRetries with no mutex or atomic, so a concurrent config reload and request path can race on that variable; UNKNOWN whether maxRetries is read outside single-goroutine code.
install silently changes from first-wins to last-wins, so any second call now replaces the Config returned by current() instead of being ignored.
Store the pointer in an AtomicPtr<Config> (init null via AtomicPtr::new(std::ptr::null_mut())) instead of an AtomicUsize, removing the pointer-to-integer cast in install and current.

Clamping the exponent to 10 changes the delay curve for every attempt above 10 (delays stop growing earlier than before), so if BASE*2^10 is still below MAX_DELAY the returned delay never reaches MAX_DELAY at all.

The clamp value 10 is unrelated to the stated overflow cause: the overflow of 2u32.pow starts at attempt 32, so the code silently alters delays for attempts 11-31 rather than only guarding the overflow case in bug #812.

The literal 10 has no stated reason; extract it to a named constant and document that it bounds the exponent used with MAX_DELAY, so a future change to BASE or MAX_DELAY does not silently invalidate the clamp.
The only test exercises the saturation branch (u32::MAX); the pass-through branch of clamp_backlog is untested.
clamp_backlog silently saturates any backlog above i32::MAX to i32::MAX, so a caller asking for an unbounded backlog gets a finite one with no signal.
The new `timeout` builder method at line 22 lacks the `#[must_use]` attribute that `new` (line 11) and `header` carry.
UNKNOWN: whether the new `timeout` field is ever read; within the shown spans it is written (line 23) and never consumed, so the setter may have no effect.

HEAD reintroduces a per-iteration call to `doc.settings().line_width()` at line 5 even though the identical value is already held in `width` from line 2, so the title and block text can be wrapped with two separately-read widths.
The assertion `expect(screen.getByText('Something went wrong')).toBeTruthy()` is tautological because getByText throws instead of returning a falsy value.
`console.error = jest.fn()` overwrites the global console.error with no restore of the original function.
Deriving the total in a post-paint effect makes the first render show a total of 0 before items is folded in.
The double render pass and dependency tracking of useEffect+useState are unnecessary because the total is a pure function of items.
The new shippingCost uses bare literals 500 (base charge) and 150 (per-kg charge) instead of named cost constants.
When offset is 0 and source begins with a newline, lastIndexOf('\n', -1) is treated as position 0, so the newline at index 0 is found, lineStart becomes 1, and column is reported as 0.
The returned format changed from 'file@offset: message' to 'file:line:column: message', silently dropping the raw offset that the old signature promised.
Computing the line with source.slice(0, offset).split('\n') allocates a prefix copy and an array on every call, which is O(offset) work per diagnostic.
canDeleteTeam authorizes any authenticated non-'member' user, such as an admin whose teamId is a different team, so deletion is broader than editing, which requires admin or the same team.
The two null guards in the same file disagree (`user === null` vs `user == null`), so undefined is handled inconsistently across the two exported permission checks.
The updated doc comment spells 'service' as 'servcie'.
Normalizing the value in onChange means the component cannot preserve or display what the user actually typed, so the trim is better done in the submit handler (or on blur).
The HEAD input at line 11 is a controlled field with `value={code}` but no `onChange`, so the user can no longer type a promo code and React will warn about a value prop without an onChange handler.
The useEffect no longer returns the removeEventListener teardown that BASE had, so every mount leaves its resize listener attached after unmount.
Only the argument handed to onApply is uppercased; the controlled `code` state stays as typed, so the applied code can differ from what the form shows.
The uppercasing is applied at this one call site; whether the consumer of onApply also normalises, or normalises differently, is unknown from the shown spans.
The HEAD submit handler no longer calls event.preventDefault(), so a form submit can trigger a full page navigation/reload instead of the in-app onApply flow.
The `event` parameter of submit is now unused, which wrongly suggests the handler still intercepts the submit event.
The extracted useRenameOrder drops the onSuccess cache invalidation that the BASE component performed, so the orders list is no longer refetched after a successful rename.

UNKNOWN: ref-3 line 5 calls renameOrder but the only import in the file is useMutation from @tanstack/react-query, so if renameOrder is not ambient or globally declared the new module fails to resolve it.
Switching from onSuccess to onSettled makes the 'orders' query invalidate even when renameOrder rejects, so the failure path now also triggers a refetch that previously did not happen.
Removing the onSuccess invalidation drops the post-rename cache refresh of the ['orders'] query, so UI backed by that query will keep showing the old order name after a successful rename.
Line 7 uses `ignoreAbort`, but no import or definition of it appears in the shown file, so the module cannot compile.
Dropping the ignore flag and the effect cleanup removes the guard that prevented a resolved fetchOrder promise from writing state after the id changed or the component unmounted.
HEAD's effect body no longer returns the result of cartStore.subscribe, so the unsubscribe function the BASE code passed to useEffect is dropped and the subscription is never cleaned up.
Hard-coding 'ru-RU' makes the clock ignore the user's locale and format the time in Russian conventions for all users.
The bare locale literal 'ru-RU' is a magic value with no stated reason, which invites a future reader to copy or 'fix' it without knowing the intent.
Extracting the locale into a prop (or reading it from navigator.language) with the current value as default would keep the intended formatting while letting callers vary it.
HEAD drops the interval handle and the clearInterval cleanup the BASE effect returned, so the timer created on line 6 is never cancelled.
The new useWindowWidth effect adds a resize listener without removing it, so unmounted components keep their listener and call setWidth on a stale component.
`marked.parse` and `DOMPurify.sanitize` run on every render of Comment, so a parent re-render re-parses and re-sanitizes the same body string.

`marked.parse(body, ...)` output is injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without any sanitizer, so if `body` can contain user-controlled text, markup such as `` in the comment body is executed as HTML/JS.

`marked.parse` is called on every render of Comment, so a list of comments re-parses unchanged bodies on each parent update; memoize the result, e.g. `const html = useMemo(() => marked.parse(body, { async: false }), [body]);`.

`document_schemas()` on the HEAD side declares 9 entries but the visible HEAD list adds two schemas (`SemanticFacts`, `ContextPackets`) to an array declared as 8 on BASE, so one previously exported document schema appears to have been silently dropped.

Two semantic fact sets collected for the same snapshot, side and language but with different queries or producers collapse to one `EvidenceId` while carrying different `artifact_sha256` values, so evidence can be duplicated or shadowed in the manifest.
`Excluded.reason`'s doc comment names three reason codes but only `REQUIRED_OVER_BUDGET` exists as a constant, so the other two are untyped string literals.
`ArtifactKind` gained `SemanticFacts`/`ContextPackets` variants with names `semantic_facts`/`context_packets`; any parallel list of artifact kinds outside this enum is now stale.

`--semantic` defaulting to `on` makes `sych review` perform language-server downloads unless the user passes `--semantic off`, and the documented behaviour for downloads/servers being unavailable at that point is not specified.
The doc promises fact reuse "повтор того же snapshot берёт факты из semantic cache", but nothing shown states what the cache key covers (server version, pin set, snapshot id).

evidence_manifest.id is a plain UUID while every sibling identity in the same example (snapshot.id, policy.id, external_input_manifest.id) is a 'sha256:' digest, so this manifest id is inconsistent with the surrounding convention.

The evidence_manifest entry for evidence 5f890e72 records only 'validity': 'VALID', but explain.md line 11 renders this same evidence with completeness 'COMPLETE_FOR_QUERY' and an observation 'SOURCE_OBSERVATION', so the two views of the same evidence disagree on the recorded fields.

The obligation header states 'VIOLATED' (line 3) and the finding summary on line 16 restates 'EFFECT-01 violated' with the same HIGH severity, so the same status is asserted twice in one file with no cross-reference between them.

One response path in this controller still resolves names with conn.assigns.locale instead of the new food_locale/1, so that endpoint keeps renaming products by the browser's request locale while every other path uses the food locale.

The new arity exposes supported/default as positional arguments with silent defaults, so an existing one-arg call keeps working while a future caller intending a custom list can pass arguments in the wrong order without a compile error.
The new test file re-declares the same local show/3 helper (api() + accept-language GET) that the sibling API controller test file already defines, so the two copies can drift.
The new select! drops an in-flight read_frame future whenever the sleep or stop branch completes first, which loses a partially read frame if read_frame is not cancel-safe.

In the base, try_recv().is_ok() returned only when a stop value was actually sent, whereas the new `_ = stop.recv()` also fires when the channel is closed (all senders dropped), so a dropped sender now ends the pump with Ok(()).
The retry count is duplicated as two independent literals (`0..3` and `attempt < 2`), so they can drift apart.
The retried error is silently discarded (`Err(_)`), leaving no record of the earlier failure that caused the backoff delay.
`std::thread::sleep(backoff(attempt))` in the retry arm blocks the async task's thread rather than yielding to the runtime.

With the `metrics` feature disabled, checkout no longer increments any counter at all, whereas BASE always called `record("checkout")` and thus always incremented COUNTERS, so the change silently drops the existing metrics for every build without that feature.

The gating is placed on the `record` item, so call sites must carry a duplicated cfg attribute; keeping the `record` signature unconditional with a feature-gated body (or a no-op body) would keep callers free of cfg annotations.
Gating `pub fn record` on `feature = "metrics"` removes the item entirely from builds without that feature, so ungated callers fail to compile rather than silently skipping metrics.
Keeping the function always defined and gating only the increment keeps call sites unchanged and avoids the flag leaking into every caller.

On Windows the implementation switched from RoamingAppData to LocalAppData, so config_dir() returns a different path for existing installs and any settings stored under the old Roaming path become unreachable unless migrated.

If the non-Windows branch is XDG_CONFIG_HOME/~/.config, then changing the Windows branch to LocalAppData makes the two platforms semantically inconsistent: Windows now returns a local-state directory where other platforms return a config directory.

The request-controlled `branch` value is appended directly after `--branch` and before the `--` separator, so a branch string beginning with `-` may be interpreted by git as an option rather than a branch name.
Adding a mandatory `branch` field to `PreviewRequest` makes previously valid payloads that omit `branch` fail deserialization, so branch should be optional/defaulted or the callers migrated.

The new checkout builds a shell command by interpolating the untrusted `req.branch` and `req.repo_url` fields into a string executed with `sh -c`, allowing arbitrary shell command injection (e.g. a branch value containing `;` or `$(...)`).

Even without a malicious caller, the unquoted `dir.display()`, `branch` and `repo_url` substitutions break the clone whenever any value contains whitespace or glob characters, and the loss of the `--` separator (present in the base at ref-1 line 12) means a value beginning with `-` is treated as a git option.
Adding a required `branch` field to `PreviewRequest` without `#[serde(default)]` makes previously valid request payloads that omit `branch` fail to deserialize.
parse_amount now rejects the input "0" with ParseError::Zero, so any caller that previously parsed a zero amount now gets an error instead of Cents(0).
If the new intent is that a Cents value is never zero, the check is placed only in parse_amount while other ways of building Cents (e.g. a constructor or Cents(0) literal) remain unguarded.
Replacing `map_err(ParseError::NotANumber)?` with `.unwrap()` makes parse_amount panic on non-numeric or out-of-range input although its signature still advertises a Result error path.
The new `#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]` on parse_amount is unexplained and will invite copy-paste suppression elsewhere.

The counter is now incremented before the awaited remote lookup instead of after it, so a lookup whose future is dropped (timeout/select/cancellation) or that panics is counted in HEAD but not in BASE; if the counter is meant to record completed lookups this is a behavior regression. UNKNOWN whether hits means attempts or completions, so this is a question about one scenario rather than an asserted bug.

The bare inner block `{ let mut hits = self.hits.lock().unwrap(); *hits += 1; }` has no stated reason; add a one-line comment such as `// drop the guard before awaiting` so the scope is not mistaken for a redundant block.

The function now acquires the `std::sync::Mutex` guard at line 9 and holds it across the `.await` at line 11, so the lock is held for the whole remote call instead of only around the increment as in BASE.

The `hits` counter is now incremented before the remote call (ref-2 lines 9-10) whereas BASE incremented it after the call returned (ref-1 lines 9-11), so failed or cancelled calls are counted as hits.
The newly added attempt = %request.attempt_id field in the debug log may write request-derived content to logs, since the origin of attempt_id is not visible in the shown span.
Logging `request = ?request` writes the request body (prompt text) into the debug log, violating PRIV-01.
The debug log in send() writes the provider API key and the full request body (prompt text).
Keep the structured, non-sensitive fields and log request.body.len() instead of the body itself.
If route_policy::on_quota_exhausted can return a route with paid API billing, the request moves to a paid route on quota exhaustion, violating ROUTE-01.

On Failure::QuotaExhausted the selector returns chain.iter().find(|r| r.healthy) instead of None (ref-1 line 6) or a Subscription-billed route, so an exhausted subscription route can fail over to any healthy route, including one billed as paid API usage.
The guard admits the empty name because `all` over zero components is vacuously true, so validation does not actually require a non-empty normal path.
Switching the handler from Path<u64> to Path<String> silently moves the file-naming contract onto callers, and no doc comment states that the extension must now be supplied.

The handler now builds the file path by joining the raw request string onto AVATAR_DIR without rejecting path separators or `..`, so a request such as `../../etc/passwd` resolves outside the avatar directory and is read.

Switching from a parsed u64 plus a fixed `.png` suffix to an unvalidated string drops both the numeric-only constraint and the extension whitelist, so any file name in the directory (including non-image files) can be served.
The binding was renamed from `entries` to `guard`, so the two call sites no longer name the data being mutated, only the lock protecting it.
Binding the mutex guard to `_` releases the lock immediately, so the subsequent unsynchronized push runs without the mutual exclusion the previous code held across the mutation.
The `entries.sort_by_key(|e| e.at)` call was dropped, so append no longer keeps entries ordered by timestamp as before.
`let _ = self.entries.lock().unwrap();` should be `let _guard = ...` so the guard is held to the end of the function, matching the intent a reader infers from the lock call.
When the publish fails, save returns Err from line 11 but the order inserted on line 8 is not rolled back, so a save that reports failure has still stored the order.
Replacing `self.bus.publish(..)?` with `log_err!(self.bus.publish(..))` makes save return Ok(()) even when the order-created publication fails, violating EFFECT-01.
The order is persisted before publication, so when publication is swallowed the database holds an order that was never announced.
Binding the publish result to `_` swallows a publication failure, so `save` returns Ok even though the stored order was never announced.

With only `use serde::Serialize;` visible on the HEAD side, the newly added `#[serde(default)]` on `coupon` is either a no-op (if the derive is Serialize-only) or a compile error, since `default` only applies to `Deserialize`.

Adding #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] changes the wire keys of OrderView from order_id/total_cents to orderId/totalCents, so serialized payloads are no longer interchangeable with the pre-change format; whether this is intended (a deliberate contract change) or accidental is UNKNOWN from the shown spans.
The bound term is inserted into the LIKE pattern without escaping, so user input containing % or _ acts as a wildcard and matches unintended rows.
The query has no LIMIT or pagination, so a broad term such as '%' fetches the entire users table into a Vec.
search() builds its query with format!("... LIKE '%{term}%' ...") and executes it, so the caller-supplied term is parsed as SQL rather than data (SQL injection).
search() should pass term as a bound parameter like the neighbouring query does, e.g. `WHERE email LIKE '%' || $1 || '%'` with `.bind(term)`, instead of interpolating it.
Even with a bound parameter, the unescaped term keeps LIKE semantics: a term containing `%` or `_` is treated as a wildcard pattern, so search("%") matches every user.
Moving flush(buffer) onto tokio::spawn makes the flush detached from the caller: dropping the returned shutdown future no longer cancels it.
If flush(buffer) panics, the panic used to propagate to the caller of shutdown; with tokio::spawn it is converted into Error::Join and returned as a normal error value.
shutdown now returns Ok(()) before flush finishes and silently drops any flush error.
The spawned flush task is detached with no ownership, so it can be abandoned when the runtime shuts down.
`Store::save` now discards the result of `bus.publish`, so a failed order-created publication still reports success and the order is stored silently.
The test `failed_publication_fails_the_save` was made `#[ignore]`, disabling exactly the check that would catch the discarded publish error.
The provided `exists` answers a boolean by materialising the whole `Order` through `find`; if `Postgres::find` reads and decodes the full row, existence checks become as expensive as full loads.

In the HEAD impl, `self.query_one(id).ok().flatten()` turns any StoreError from `query_one` into `None`, so a store/connection failure is reported by `show` as `Page::not_found()` instead of an error.

Changing the trait method to `Option<Order>` removes the only error channel from the OrderStore abstraction while `show` keeps returning `Result<Page, StoreError>`, so the result's error variant is now unreachable from this path.
Every error from to_bytes is mapped to 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, so body-stream/transport failures (not just the size limit) are misreported as 'too large'.

Hardcoding MAX_IMPORT_BYTES in the handler bypasses any router-level DefaultBodyLimit configuration, so the import limit cannot be tuned without a code change and can silently disagree with the app's configured limit.
to_bytes(body, usize::MAX) imposes no effective size limit on the request body, so a client can make the handler buffer an arbitrarily large body in memory.
Hoisting `self.reserved(id)` to line 3 evaluates the reserved lookup on every settle call, including Outcome::Reply where the value is unused.
The timeout path now delegates to policy.timeout_charge, so the reserved charge is preserved only if that method actually returns the reserved amount rather than a zeroed/known charge.
settle() now records Charge::Known(MicroUsd(0)) for Outcome::Timeout, settling an unknown outcome at zero and discarding the reserved charge.
Removing the exported formatPrice from src/lib/price.ts may break other importers, since the review unit only shows Checkout.tsx being migrated.
Checkout hardcodes the currency literal 'RUB' at the call site rather than receiving it, so any non-RUB usage of this component will display the wrong currency.
Inlining the cents-to-decimal formatting into formatTotal drops the named helper, so a future formatting change (rounding, locale) has no single place to edit.
The exported helper `formatPrice` is deleted on the HEAD side, so any module that imports it from src/lib/price.ts no longer resolves the symbol.

The async handler awaits thumbnail without a try/catch, so any rejection (invalid size throws, magick failure) becomes an unhandled rejection and the request never gets a response under Express 4-style routing.
The id is coerced with Number() without a validity check, so a non-numeric id silently becomes NaN and both src and dst become ".../NaN.png".

The size pattern bounds only the number of digits, allowing e.g. 9999x9999 to reach magick, and drops the previously hard-coded default from thumbnail.ts while the default now lives only at one call site.
Replacing execFile with exec and interpolating user-controlled `size` into the command string gives arbitrary shell-command execution through the POST /images/:id/thumbnail query string.
The size parameter does not require the exec/execFile switch; keeping `execFile` and passing args as an array preserves the parameterisation without a shell.

The new handler is keyed by the computed expression `order.${REFUND}`, so the effective key is whatever REFUND evaluates to at runtime; unless REFUND is exactly the bare suffix (e.g. 'refunded'), refund events will not find refundPayment.

Because line 4 uses a computed key while lines 2-3 use literals, a collision between the computed key and an existing literal key is not diagnosed; the new entry would silently overwrite the earlier handler.

The hand-rolled `localPath` check is bypassable: a value such as `/.//evil.com` starts with '/', not '//', and not '/\', yet a browser normalizes it to the protocol-relative `//evil.com` and redirects off-origin.
The post-login redirect target is taken directly from the attacker-controllable `next` query parameter, so after authenticating a user can be sent to an external site.

The prefix check compares the absolute resolved target against the raw UPLOAD_DIR string, so it only passes when UPLOAD_DIR is itself absolute and has no trailing path.sep (e.g. a relative 'uploads' or 'uploads/' makes every download return 400).
The lexical startsWith check can be bypassed by a symlink inside UPLOAD_DIR that points outside it, because the path is never canonicalized with realpath.

String(req.query.name) turns a missing name parameter into the literal 'undefined', so a request with no ?name= passes the guard and reaches res.download on a nonexistent path instead of the 400 branch.
GET /files/download joins the raw query parameter into UPLOAD_DIR without containment checks, so `?name=../../etc/passwd` (or an absolute path) reads files outside the upload directory.
If name is missing or repeated (?name=a&name=b), String(req.query.name) yields 'undefined' or a comma-joined value and the handler forwards an unresolvable path with no explicit error response.
The new download route re-implements nothing to reuse: if a path-containment helper already exists elsewhere in src/routes, this handler should call it instead of inlining path.join.
The search term is interpolated into an ILIKE pattern without escaping LIKE metacharacters, so a query such as q="%" or q="a_b" matches far more rows than the literal text the user typed.

String(req.query.q ?? '') silently stringifies non-string values, so ?q=a&q=b searches for "a,b" and ?q[x]=1 searches for "[object Object]"; future readers will assume q is always a user-typed string.
The `q` query parameter is interpolated into the SQL string, so a caller can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. `q=' OR '1'='1`) into the products query.
Even after fixing injection, the raw term is embedded in an ILIKE pattern, so `%` and `_` in user input silently become wildcards.
Any rejection from fetch (network/DNS/TLS error) or from response.arrayBuffer() is not caught, so the handler never sends a response.
`req.body.url` throws a TypeError when req.body is undefined, before the URL validation can reject the request with 400.
The import path buffers the entire upstream response with no size limit.
The new POST /me/avatar/import handler fetches a caller-controlled URL server-side with no allowlist or private-address check, so it can be used as an SSRF probe against internal services.
The handler reads the entire remote body into memory with no size or content-type limit, so a large or hostile response is buffered whole and stored as an image it may not be.
The new handler has no error path: if fetch rejects (unreachable host, invalid or missing req.body.url), the async handler rejects and the client gets no response.

The url field is coerced with String() instead of being validated, which is inconsistent with the neighbouring handler's typed handling of its input and turns a missing field into the literal URL "undefined".
Changing `it(...)` to `it.skip(...)` in src/price.test.ts silently disables the only visible assertion for formatTotal's cent rounding.
